title: How Blake Anderson scaled Cal AI and UMAX with organic creators and co-founders
summary: Blake Anderson explains how he went from a failed college marketplace app to RizzGPT, UMAX and Cal AI by building on human insecurities and scaling organic creator content. He covers vetting creators by comment-section quality, taking many outreach shots, choosing distribution before product, co-founder equity, and optimizing for learning.

principles.text: Build products around core human insecurities or desires; virality then comes built in, instead of forcing a clever use case to go viral.
principles.quote: taking these core human sort of insecurities or desires and um, orienting a product around that as opposed to figuring out some sort of like overintellectualized use case thing

principles.text: Take far more shots with creators: DM hundreds a day instead of fixating on a few names.
principles.quote: if you're not DMing hundreds of influencers per day and you're asking yourself why you can't set up partnerships, you're not taking enough shots.

principles.text: Pick creators by engaged comment sections (thoughtful replies, liked comments), not followers or raw views.
principles.quote: what I index for within my companies is what creators have really engaged comment sections.

principles.text: Know your distribution strategy before building; it shapes product and pricing (paid ads suit higher price points, organic suits lower).
principles.quote: it is very helpful to know what your distribution strategy is going into something.

principles.text: Great co-founders multiply the business; an equal split keeps everyone incentivized and captures more upside.
principles.quote: I think that great co-founders are multipliers on the business.

principles.text: Optimize every project for learning so even failure leaves you with transferable skills.
principles.quote: one for me at least is to optimize for learning everything that I do
